title: Mentioning specific household details like children or housing status may accelerate funding regardless of gender.
Pitches from women that explicitly reference previous loans from the NWTF institution are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who address lenders directly in their pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide detailed breakdowns of their children's status fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include explicit gratitude markers or promises to repay may fund more slowly.
Pitches that include precise currency amounts or specific numerical quantities tend to fund more slowly for both men and women.
Emphasizing a long duration of business experience or longevity predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches from women that include details about the employment or social status of a spouse or partner are associated with increased funding speed.
Pitches from women that describe the borrower using terms like 'hardworking' or 'entrepreneur' are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who emphasize a longer duration of business ownership fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their family fund faster.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention marital status or personal hardships fund more slowly.
